instructions:
RooQuiz: lightweight assessment platform for lead capture and viral sharing, not formal exams.

SCENES (set at creation, immutable):
- knowledge_quiz: scored exam; each question carries score + correctAnswer.
- scored_quiz: put a score on each choices[i] (Option Scoring); report.formula combines question codes.
- outcome_quiz: "which X are you" typing quiz, no scores. Define types in report.outcomes, then every choice votes via choices[i].outcomes (TrueFalse uses trueOutcomes/falseOutcomes); most-voted type wins.

CODES: every question has a stable `code`. Formulas, dimensionAnalysis and every question edit reference it. Call get_form first to read the current codes — never guess or invent one.

TERMINOLOGY: "examinee" and "respondent" are the same thing — the person who answers a quiz. The product UI calls them Respondents; the tools and fields keep the examinee wording (list_examinees / get_examinee / update_examinee, examineeId). A user asking about respondents means these tools.

FASTEST PATH: check list_templates and use create_form_from_template when a suitable template exists; reach for create_form only for genuinely new material.

TRANSLATIONS: a form has ONE source structure plus a primary `language`. Every other language is a translation mirroring that source — identical codes, only human-readable text differs. Change structure on the source form; change wording via update_form_translation.

MASKED PII: read tools return respondent name / email / phone-typed custom fields masked (J*n, j***g@example.com, +86 138****8000), and so are email addresses or phone numbers a respondent typed into their answers. Masking is irreversible. Relay masked values to the user as-is, never pass one back as an argument, and never write one back. Address a respondent by examineeId, a submission by its record id, a lead by its leadId.

TEAM SCOPE: every tool acts on the team this token is bound to (get_active_tenant / switch_active_tenant).

BATCHING: assign_leads and set_lead_tags accept many ids per call — pass them all at once instead of looping one call per lead.

tools.name: create_form
tools.description: Create a form in the team this token is bound to. Pass the questions array and report configuration in one call instead of following up with per-question calls. In the outcome_quiz scene report.outcomes is REQUIRED at create time (TrueFalse votes via trueOutcomes/falseOutcomes). The returned structuredContent.fields carries each question code — read those first, then fill in a scored_quiz report.formula (e.g. q_a + q_b) or a report.dimensionAnalysis via update_form / set_dimension_analysis. Creates the primary language only; add other languages with create_form_translation. Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

scene.description: quiz=exam, scored_quiz=scored_quiz, outcome=typing quiz (votes decide which outcome type wins)

description.description: Optional form description. Allows description-scope rich text (including ). This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

questions.description: Optional. A list of questions/page breaks to create at once, written into form.fields in order. Question types: SingleCheck/MultiCheck/TrueFalse; FillBlank (free text — scored in quiz via correctAnswer, an unscored data-collection field in scored_quiz); DropDown (single or multiple via `multiple`, use it instead of SingleCheck/MultiCheck when there are more than 20 choices); Cascade (hierarchical choices via children, scored_quiz only); Ordering (quiz only, correctAnswer = all choices in the correct order); DateField/TimeField as unscored data-collection fields (scored_quiz only); NumberField (quiz: optional numeric correctAnswer + score; scored_quiz: the submitted number feeds report formulas); Rate (scored_quiz only, the 1..steps rating value is the question score unless per-star scores are set in the web app). Insert a page break with { type: "Breaker" }, which the AI can interleave between questions to paginate. At most 100 items.

items.description: One question, or a page break. FIELD APPLICABILITY — `type` is the only field the schema always requires; `type` (plus the form scene) decides which of the remaining fields apply, and one that does not apply is either rejected with an explanatory error or ignored, so never pass it. Breaker (page break) takes nothing but `type`. Every question type takes `name` (required) plus the optional `code` / `description` / `explain` / `required`. Type-specific fields: SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering / Cascade need `choices` (Cascade nests via choices[i].children; DropDown also takes `multiple`; Ordering also takes `shuffle`); TrueFalse has a fixed pair of options and takes `trueLabel` / `falseLabel` instead of `choices`; DateField / TimeField take `precision`; NumberField takes `min` / `max` / `unit` / `decimalPlaces`; Rate takes `steps` / `words`. Scene rules for scoring: quiz — `correctAnswer` plus `score` > 0 are REQUIRED on SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering, optional on FillBlank (add `aiMatch` to have AI grade it instead of exact string match) and NumberField (omit both and the question is just a data-collection field), and rejected on DateField / TimeField; scored_quiz — score each option via choices[i].score; `correctAnswer` / `score` are rejected on NumberField and Rate (the submitted value is the score) and on FillBlank (free text is collected only, never scored); outcome — nothing is scored: `correctAnswer` / `score` / `aiMatch` are all rejected, every choice needs `outcomes` (TrueFalse votes via `trueOutcomes` / `falseOutcomes`). Type availability per scene: Ordering is knowledge_quiz-only; FillBlank works in knowledge_quiz (optionally scored) and in scored_quiz (data-collection only — its answer never feeds a score or a report formula); Cascade, Rate, DateField and TimeField are scored_quiz-only; and the outcome_quiz scene accepts only SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / TrueFalse / Breaker.

type.description: Question type; Breaker means a page break (the frontend pushes subsequent questions to the next page), no name/choices etc. needed

code.description: Optional stable identifier for this question (field code). Omit it to let the server auto-generate one. Set a meaningful code (e.g. "q1") when report.formula or a dimension needs to reference this question, so you can write the formula as `{{q1}}` in the same call instead of round-tripping via get_form. Rules: start with a letter or underscore, then only letters/digits/underscores (no hyphens, spaces, or leading digit), at most 64 chars, and not a reserved math word (e, E, pi, PI, tau, phi, i, Infinity, NaN, true, false, null, undefined). Must be unique among all items in the form.

Do not stuff the answer explanation into description — that is the question's supplementary note and will not be shown as an explanation to respondents/graders.

required.description: Whether the question is required, default false

precision.description: DateField / TimeField only: picker precision. DateField accepts year | month | day | hour | minute | second (default day; e.g. "month" shows a year-month picker, "second" a full datetime picker). TimeField accepts only minute | second (default minute). Ignored for other question types.

min.description: NumberField only: minimum allowed input value (respondents cannot submit a smaller number). Rejected for other question types.

max.description: NumberField only: maximum allowed input value (must be >= min). Rejected for other question types.

unit.description: NumberField only: display unit suffix shown after the input, e.g. "kg" / "$" / "min". Rejected for other question types.

decimalPlaces.description: NumberField only: how many decimal places respondents may enter (stored as the field's numeric precision), default 0 = integers only. Rejected for other question types. Note this is different from the string `precision` of DateField / TimeField.

steps.description: Rate only: number of rating steps, i.e. the highest rating (3-10, default 5). In the scored_quiz scene the submitted rating value (1..steps) is the question score, unless a per-star score is configured in the web app. Rejected for other question types.

words.description: Rate only: optional scale labels evenly distributed under the rating control, e.g. ["Poor", "Excellent"] for the two endpoints (up to 5 labels). Rejected for other question types.

choices.description: Choice-based questions only (SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering / Cascade), where it is required; ignored for every other type, including TrueFalse — its two options come from trueLabel / falseLabel. Per-type limits: SingleCheck / MultiCheck 2-20 items — for a longer list use DropDown (2-100 items) instead; Ordering 2-10 items; Cascade nests via choices[i].children (up to 3 levels, at most 100 nodes in total). IMPORTANT (knowledge_quiz scene): vary the position of the correct option(s) across questions — do NOT always place the correct answer first. Distribute correct answers roughly evenly over all positions so they are not predictable.

multiple.description: DropDown only: allow selecting multiple options (default false = single select). Affects the quiz-scene correctAnswer shape: an array of labels/codes when true, a single one when false. Rejected for other question types (SingleCheck/MultiCheck are inherently single/multi).

shuffle.description: Ordering only: shuffle the displayed choice order for each respondent. Defaults to true for MCP-created questions — the stored choices order would otherwise leak the correct order when correctAnswer matches it. Pass false only when the initial order is intentionally meaningful. Rejected for other question types.

trueOutcomes.description: Outcome scene + TrueFalse only (required there together with falseOutcomes): the outcome codes that answering "true" votes for. Use [] for a side that votes for nothing. Rejected for other question types / scenes.

falseOutcomes.description: Outcome scene + TrueFalse only (required there together with trueOutcomes): the outcome codes that answering "false" votes for. Use [] for a side that votes for nothing. Rejected for other question types / scenes.

trueLabel.description: TrueFalse only: custom display text for the "true" option (e.g. "Yes" / "Agree"). Ignored for other question types. Leave empty to fall back to the built-in default for the form language ("Correct" in English forms). Does not change the stored answer value, which stays "true".

falseLabel.description: TrueFalse only: custom display text for the "false" option (e.g. "No" / "Disagree"). Ignored for other question types. Leave empty to fall back to the built-in default for the form language ("Incorrect" in English forms). Does not change the stored answer value, which stays "false".

anyOf.description: SingleCheck / single-select DropDown: one choice label or code. FillBlank: the standard answer text.
MultiCheck / multi-select DropDown (multiple=true): the label or code of every correct choice. Ordering: ALL choice labels/codes in the correct order (order-sensitive).
NumberField: a finite number, matched exactly.

correctAnswer.description: The "correct answer" of the knowledge_quiz scene; setting it makes the question scored, so pair it with a positive `score`. The shape follows the question type — see the anyOf branches; a choice is referenced by its label or its code, so reference it by code whenever the same label appears more than once (Ordering rejects an ambiguous label outright). Required on SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering in the knowledge_quiz scene, optional on FillBlank / NumberField there. NumberField answers must be typeable within min / max and decimalPlaces. Rejected for DateField / TimeField / Rate (data-collection and rating fields; configure date/time scoring in the web app), rejected for FillBlank in the scored_quiz scene (free text is collected only there), and rejected in the outcome_quiz scene (no right or wrong answers there). In the scored_quiz scene prefer choices[i].score per option; passing correctAnswer + score there only falls back to "the matching choice gets score, others get 0".

score.description: Points this question is worth, default 0 (not scored). Quiz scene: awarded when the answer matches correctAnswer, and a positive value is required once correctAnswer is set. Scored Quiz scene: pairing it with correctAnswer enables the fallback mode above, but choices[i].score is more flexible. Rejected in the outcome_quiz scene, for DateField / TimeField / Rate, and — in the scored_quiz scene — for NumberField (where the submitted number itself is the score) and FillBlank (collected only, never scored).

aiMatch.description: Only for FillBlank in the knowledge_quiz scene. Enables AI grading: the AI compares the respondent answer against correctAnswer and scores by accuracy, instead of requiring an exact string match. Requires correctAnswer (the standard answer) and score > 0 (the score earned when accuracy reaches the threshold). Pass an empty object {} to enable with default settings; omit for plain exact-match grading.

accuracy.description: Accuracy threshold (0-100) at or above which the full score is awarded. Default 80.

extraLevels.description: Optional partial-credit tiers for answers below the full-score threshold. Each {accuracy, score}: if the AI accuracy is below the threshold but >= this tier accuracy, this score is awarded. Tiers are matched from highest accuracy to lowest; if none match, the score is 0.

score.description: Score awarded at this tier

report.description: Report configuration. knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz: overallAnalysis fields are flat at the top level and dimensionAnalysis is nested (strongly recommended for the scored_quiz scene, optional for the knowledge_quiz scene). outcome: only the outcomes key is allowed, and it is required at create time.

title.description: Overall analysis title, default "Overall Scored Quiz Analysis"

formula.description: Total-score formula for the scored_quiz scene, and the ONLY source of the overall score there — summing question scores is the knowledge_quiz rule, so a scored_quiz without this formula scores null and no level ever matches. Required whenever levels are set. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` for custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. Supported operators: + - * / ( ); every referenced code must exist in the current form. Setting dimension formulas does NOT cover this — the overall formula is separate.

summaryTemplate.description: Summary template. Allows description-scope rich text (headings/lists/links/images/ etc.). Supports math formulas: write ``, rendered by KaTeX on the frontend. Supports variable placeholders `` (cid can be score / level / a question code). This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

suggestionsTemplate.description: Suggestions template; same rich-text rules as summaryTemplate.

hideOverallScore.description: Hide the overall score on the result page (the score ring / number / percentile), keeping the level name, level description and summary. Scored scenes only (ignored for outcome). Default false.

levels.description: Score levels (at most 20), ordered by upper bound ascending. Example: [{label:"Needs improvement",upTo:60},{label:"Good",upTo:80},{label:"Excellent"}] means (-∞,60) / [60,80) / [80,+∞). The last level must omit upTo. In the scored_quiz scene these levels are matched against the formula score, so formula must be set alongside them (rejected otherwise).

upTo.description: Upper bound (exclusive); omit for the last level

cta.description: Optional CTA button shown on the result page when the score falls in this level (e.g. "Book a consultation" for the low band). Providing it enables the button. Overall levels only — dimension levels reject it.

newWindow.description: Open the link in a new window, default false

dimensionAnalysis.description: Multi-dimension analysis (radar chart + per-dimension breakdown). Each dimension gets a server-generated code returned in structuredContent. In the knowledge_quiz scene set fieldCodes per dimension; in the scored_quiz scene set a formula. Dimensions reference question codes: if you set custom question codes you can configure dimensions in the same create_form call; otherwise create the questions first, then get_form to read the auto-generated codes.

showRadarChart.description: Whether to show the radar chart, default true

showStandardLine.description: Whether to show the standard-score line on the radar chart

dimensions.description: The dimension list (at most 50). Pass an empty array (or omit) to mean "no dimensions".

standardScore.description: Standard score (the radar-chart standard line; in the scored_quiz scene it also acts as the dimension full mark). Default 0.

fieldCodes.description: Required in the knowledge_quiz scene: the question codes this dimension covers (dimension score = sum of these field scores). Each code must exist in the form. Ignored in the scored_quiz scene.

formula.description: Required in the scored_quiz scene: the dimension score formula. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` when you set custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. Supported operators: + - * / ( ). Ignored in the knowledge_quiz scene.

weight.description: Weight (used when computing weighted overall score), default 1

levels.description: Optional dimension levels (at most 20), ordered by upper bound ascending. Example: [{label:"Weak",upTo:60},{label:"Strong"}]. The last level must omit upTo.

upTo.description: Upper bound (exclusive); omit for the last level

outcomes.description: Outcome scene only (required there at create time, 1-50 items): the outcome types this quiz can result in. Each question choice votes for outcome codes; the outcome with the most votes wins (ties resolved by array order, earlier wins). Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz scenes.

name.description: Outcome display name shown on the result page, e.g. "Lion — The Decisive Leader". Plain text.

color.description: Theme color of this outcome, e.g. "#4caf50". Optional.

Required on SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering in the knowledge_quiz scene, optional on FillBlank / NumberField there. NumberField answers must be typeable within min / max and decimalPlaces. Rejected for DateField / TimeField / Rate (data-collection and rating fields; configure date/time scoring in the web app), rejected for FillBlank in the scored_quiz scene (free text is collected only there), and rejected in the outcome_quiz scene (no right or wrong answers there). In the scored_quiz scene prefer choices[i].score per option; passing correctAnswer + score there only falls back to "the matching choice gets score, others get 0".

score.description: Points this question is worth, default 0 (not scored). Quiz scene: awarded when the answer matches correctAnswer, and a positive value is required once correctAnswer is set. Scored Quiz scene: pairing it with correctAnswer enables the fallback mode above, but choices[i].score is more flexible. Rejected in the outcome_quiz scene, for DateField / TimeField / Rate, and — in the scored_quiz scene — for NumberField (where the submitted number itself is the score) and FillBlank (collected only, never scored).

aiMatch.description: Only for FillBlank in the knowledge_quiz scene. email.description: Address the invite was sent to

inviteUrl.description: The invite link that was emailed — you may relay it to the user

tools.name: list_leads
tools.description: List the leads (CRM records) of the current team — one lead per respondent across all forms, carrying follow-up status, assignee, colour tags, submission count and the next upcoming booking. Newest activity first by default. Filter by status / assignee / tags / created-at range / keyword / whether they have an upcoming booking. Status codes and tag codes are team-defined — call list_lead_settings first to get the valid ones, never guess. Reference a lead by its leadId and a respondent by examineeId, never by a masked email.

status.description: Filter by follow-up status code (see list_lead_settings), optional

assigneeId.description: Filter by the assigned member userId (see list_lead_settings.assignableMembers). Pass "me" for the current token's own user. Optional.

tagCodes.description: Filter by colour tag codes; a lead matches if it has ANY of them (OR). Optional.

keyword.description: Fuzzy match on the respondent's name or email. Matching runs server-side against the real values, so you can search by a full or partial email even though results come back masked.

createdFrom.description: Only leads created on/after this ISO datetime, optional

createdTo.description: Only leads created strictly before this ISO datetime (half-open), optional

hasUpcomingBooking.description: true = only leads with an active upcoming booking, false = only those without. Omit to not filter. Note: this filters within the page, so counts stay on the unfiltered basis.

sort.description: Sort order, default -lastRecordAt (most recent submission first)

leadId.description: Lead id — address a lead by this, never by a masked email

tags.description: Colour tag codes on this lead

recordCount.description: How many times this respondent submitted

respondent.description: The respondent { id, examineeId, email, name, customData, ... }, PII masked

assignee.description: The member handling this lead as { id, email, username }, or null

firstForm.description: The quiz that first captured this lead as { id, title }

nextBooking.description: The next active booking of this respondent, or null

lastRecordAt.description: ISO datetime of the most recent submission

Optionally include the respondent's submission history (which quizzes they took, with score / level), the team's internal follow-up comments, and the change timeline (status / assignee / tag changes plus submissions). Reference a lead by its leadId and a respondent by examineeId, never by a masked email.

leadId.description: The lead id (the leadId returned by list_leads)

includeRecords.description: Include the respondent's submission history (default true)

includeComments.description: Include the internal follow-up comments written by team members (default false)

includeActivities.description: Include the change timeline: status / assignee / tag changes and submissions (default false)

leadId.description: Lead id — address a lead by this, never by a masked email

tags.description: Colour tag codes on this lead

recordCount.description: How many times this respondent submitted

respondent.description: The respondent { id, examineeId, email, name, customData, ... }, PII masked

assignee.description: The member handling this lead as { id, email, username }, or null

firstForm.description: The quiz that first captured this lead as { id, title }

nextBooking.description: The next active booking of this respondent, or null

firstRecordAt.description: ISO datetime of the first submission

records.description: Submission history as { totalDocs, items } (unless includeRecords was false)

tools.name: list_lead_settings
tools.description: Read the current team's lead configuration: the follow-up status codes (with label and colour, in display order), the colour tag library, and the members a lead can be assigned to. Call this before update_lead / set_lead_tags / assign_leads — status codes, tag codes and member ids are all team-specific and the write tools reject unknown values.

code.description: Status code — pass this to update_lead

builtIn.description: Whether it is one of the built-in statuses

code.description: Tag code — pass this to set_lead_tags

userId.description: Member userId — pass this to assign_leads

assignableMembers.description: Active non-viewer members a lead can be assigned to

tools.name: update_lead
tools.description: Move one lead of the current team to another follow-up status (e.g. new → contacted). The change is recorded on the lead's timeline. Status codes and tag codes are team-defined — call list_lead_settings first to get the valid ones, never guess.

leadId.description: The lead id (the leadId returned by list_leads)

status.description: The target status code, must be one of list_lead_settings.statuses[].code

tools.name: assign_leads
tools.description: Assign one or more leads of the current team to a member, or clear the assignee. Pass every lead id in a single call (up to 50) — do not loop one call per lead. The assignee must be an active non-viewer member (see list_lead_settings.assignableMembers); pass "me" for yourself, or omit / null to unassign. Each change is recorded on the lead's timeline, and the assignee gets one aggregated notification for the whole batch.

leadIds.description: The lead ids to assign, max 50 per call

assigneeId.description: The member userId to assign to, or "me" for the current token's own user. Omit (or pass null) to clear the assignee.
The member they were assigned to, or null when cleared

tools.name: set_lead_tags
tools.description: Set the colour tags on one or more leads of the current team. Pass every lead id in a single call (up to 50) — do not loop. mode: "replace" (default, overwrite the whole tag set — for editing a single lead), "add" or "remove" (for batches, where each lead has different tags and overwriting would wipe other people's tags). Tag codes must exist in the team's tag library (see list_lead_settings.tags); "remove" also accepts stale codes. Changes are recorded on each lead's timeline.

leadIds.description: The lead ids to tag, max 50 per call

tags.description: The tag codes to apply, from list_lead_settings.tags[].code

mode.description: How to apply the tags, default replace

tools.name: add_lead_comment
tools.description: Write an internal follow-up note on a lead of the current team (visible to team members only, never to the respondent). Max 2000 characters. Optionally attach the record id of the submission the note is about, as context. Read existing notes with get_lead(includeComments: true). Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

leadId.description: The lead id (the leadId returned by list_leads)

recordId.description: Optional record id this note is about (as returned by get_lead records / list_records)

leadId.description: The lead it was written on

tools.name: get_form_share_info
tools.description: Everything needed to put a form of the current team in front of an audience: the public answer link (also per language version), the team's custom domain and whether it is actually serving, ready-to-paste embed snippets in three modes (inline / popup / iframe), and the current delivery settings so you can tell whether the form will even accept responses. Pass utmSource to get every link and snippet tagged for one channel. Use this to answer "give me the link / the embed code" and to sanity-check a launch; change the switches with update_form_settings.

utmSource.description: Optional channel tag applied to the links and snippets (letters, digits, _ and - only, max 64). Omitted or invalid = no tag, in which case the embed script forwards whatever utm_* the host page already has.

iframeHeight.description: Optional pixel height for the iframe snippet, default 600

popupButtonText.description: Optional label for the popup-mode button; empty uses the built-in default

publicToken.description: Token behind the public answer link

shareUrl.description: The link to hand out (custom domain when one is serving)

defaultShareUrl.description: The same quiz on the default domain — always works

slug.description: Custom path under the custom domain; only shapes shareUrl while that domain is serving

customDomain.description: Custom-domain state { domain, status, serving, plan }

isPrimary.description: Whether this is the form primary language

embed.description: Copy-paste embed snippets { inline, popup, iframe }; null when the form has no public token

delivery.description: Delivery state: { isActive, submissionAccess, reportGateRequireCode, timeLimit, sharing, answerSheet, booking, gaTrackingId, sharedWithAll }; get_form_share_info adds the team-level examineeSignupDisabled (respondent self-signup off = a login-gated quiz turns away anyone not on the roster)

tools.name: update_form_settings
tools.description: Change how a form of the current team is delivered, as opposed to what it says (use update_form for title / questions / report / theme). Editable: submissionAccess (who may answer and whether seeing the report needs a login — this is the lead-capture gate), reportGateRequireCode (whether that login gate collects an emailed verification code, trading completion rate against lead quality), timeLimit, sharing (the result-page share button and personalised share card, which is what drives organic spread), answerSheet, booking (the result-page booking block that feeds the 1:1 call queue), gaTrackingId, sharedWithAll (whether every team member can see this form), and slug (the custom path that gives the public link a memorable, SEO-friendly address). Only the keys you pass are changed. Read the current values with get_form_share_info.

submissionAccess.description: public = anyone answers and sees the report; login_to_view_report = anyone answers but must sign in to see the report (the default, this is how leads get captured); examinee_only = a login is required before answering at all

reportGateRequireCode.description: Only applies when submissionAccess is login_to_view_report. false (the default for newly created quizzes) = the respondent only types an email and a name to see this one result — far more people finish, but the address is unverified and they get no account, and since result links do get forwarded, the report is effectively as reachable as public for whoever opens the link first. true = the respondent must confirm an emailed 6-digit code, so every captured lead has a verified address and the respondent gets an account they can return to. Quizzes created before this setting existed read as true.

sharing.description: Result-page sharing: the share button, the personalised share card and the public summary. Turning this off stops respondents spreading their results.

answerSheet.description: The answer-sheet sidebar on the answering page

enabled.description: Whether the result page offers booking a 1:1 call

booking.description: The result-page booking block. The bookable hours live in the team's booking settings, not here — this is only the switch and the copy. Bookings that come in are handled with list_bookings / review_booking.

gaTrackingId.description: Google Analytics measurement id (G-XXXXXX) or Universal Analytics id (UA-XXXX-Y). Pass an empty string to clear.

sharedWithAll.description: Whether every member of the team can see and open this form

slug.description: Custom path of the public answer link — the SEO-friendly address (e.g. quizster.app/<team>/burnout-test on the platform domain, or <custom-domain>/burnout-test when the team's custom domain is serving). Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2-64 chars, must start and end with a letter or digit, unique within the team. Pass an empty string to clear back to the random address. Changing it breaks the previous custom path right away, but the token address (/a/<publicToken>) always keeps working and the page's canonical URL follows the custom path.
Custom path after this change; null when cleared (back to the random address)

delivery.description: Delivery state: { isActive, submissionAccess, reportGateRequireCode, timeLimit, sharing, answerSheet, booking, gaTrackingId, sharedWithAll }; get_form_share_info adds the team-level examineeSignupDisabled (respondent self-signup off = a login-gated quiz turns away anyone not on the roster)

tools.name: list_bookings
tools.description: List the 1:1 bookings (discovery calls / consultations booked from a quiz report page) of the current team, earliest first. Each item carries the time range, status, meeting type, the attendee, the source quiz and submission, and the lead owner who should handle it. Filter by status / quiz / respondent / time range. Typical use: status "pending" lists the approval queue waiting on someone. Reference a booking by its bookingId; the attendee name / email come back masked.

status.description: Filter by status. pending = a request awaiting approval (the team has requireApproval on), scheduled = a confirmed meeting, the rest are terminal. Optional.

formId.description: Only bookings that came from this quiz, optional

examineeId.description: Only bookings by this respondent — the internal examinee id (get_lead's respondent.id), not the examineeId business code. Optional.

recordId.description: Only bookings tied to this submission record, optional

from.description: Only bookings starting on/after this ISO datetime, optional

to.description: Only bookings starting strictly before this ISO datetime, optional

sort.description: Sort by start time, default startAt (earliest first)

bookingId.description: Booking id — address a booking by this

timezone.description: Timezone the slot was booked in

examinee.description: The respondent behind this booking, PII masked

form.description: The quiz the booking came from

record.description: The submission the booking is tied to

items.description: The page of bookings (earliest first by default)

tools.name: get_booking_availability
tools.description: Read the current team's bookable time slots in a date range, computed from the team's weekly booking rules minus what is already taken. Returns enabled:false when the team has booking switched off or the plan does not include it. Pass bookingId to get the slots for rescheduling that booking (its own slot is not counted as taken) — always call this before reschedule_booking, since a start time outside the available slots is rejected. The range is clamped server-side if you ask for too many days.

bookingId.description: Optional: compute availability for rescheduling this booking, excluding the slot it currently occupies. Omit to see availability for the team as a whole.

enabled.description: false when the team has booking off or the plan does not include it

requireApproval.description: Whether new requests need approval (returned when booking is off)

slots.description: Bookable start times as ISO datetimes — reschedule_booking only accepts one of these

tools.name: review_booking
tools.description: Approve or decline a pending booking request of the current team. Approving turns it into a confirmed meeting and sends the attendee the confirmation with the meeting address; declining sends a short "not approved" note with the optional reason. Only works on a booking whose status is pending, and a request whose meeting time has already passed can only be declined. On approval you may set the meeting link / instructions for this one meeting (leave empty to fall back to the team-level settings). Only the team owner / admin or the lead owner can review.

bookingId.description: The booking id (the bookingId returned by list_bookings)

decision.description: approve = confirm the meeting and release the address; decline = reject the request

meetingLink.description: Approve only: the meeting URL for this meeting. Empty falls back to the team setting.

meetingInstructions.description: Approve only: how to join / what to prepare, max 1000 chars. Empty falls back to the team setting.

declineReason.description: Decline only: the reason shown to the attendee, max 500 chars. Optional.

status.description: scheduled after approving, cancelled after declining

tools.name: update_booking_status
tools.description: Close out a confirmed booking of the current team: mark it completed, mark the attendee as a no-show, or cancel it. Only works on a booking whose status is scheduled; completed / no_show additionally require the meeting to have already started. Cancelling notifies the attendee by email and fires the booking.cancelled integration event; completed / no_show are internal bookkeeping and do not contact the attendee. To handle a pending request use review_booking instead.

bookingId.description: The booking id (the bookingId returned by list_bookings)

status.description: completed = the meeting happened, no_show = the attendee did not turn up, cancelled = call it off and notify them

bookingId.description: The booking that was closed out

cancelledAt.description: ISO datetime, set when the booking was cancelled

tools.name: reschedule_booking
tools.description: Move a confirmed booking of the current team to a different time, as the organiser. The new start time must be one of the available slots — call get_booking_availability with this bookingId first and pick a startAt from its slots. The attendee is emailed about the new time, the 24h reminder is re-armed, and the booking.rescheduled integration event fires. Only works on a scheduled booking; it is rejected if the slot got taken in the meantime or if that respondent already has another active booking.

bookingId.description: The booking id (the bookingId returned by list_bookings)

startAt.description: The new start time, ISO datetime — must be one of the slots from get_booking_availability
